skill.name: ux-researcher-designer
skill.description: Generate heuristic UX personas from prepared user records and interview insights, including behaviors, needs, scenarios, confidence labels, and design implications.
skill.summary: Turn structured research inputs into evidence-aware persona drafts and design implications.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive because Markdown backticks format a documented Python command and do not invoke Ruby or a shell. The local script has no subprocess, network, credential, or filesystem behavior, and no semantic threats or prompt injection were found.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 22 uses Markdown backticks to format a fixed local Python command. It is documentation, not Ruby or shell backtick execution, and it exposes no command injection path.

content.user_title: Turn UX Research into Actionable Personas
content.value_statement: Research data can be difficult to synthesize into clear design direction. This skill generates structured personas, scenarios, confidence labels, and design implications from user records.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes usage frequency, feature adoption, devices, contexts, and pain points from prepared user records.
Classifies a dataset as power user, casual user, business user, or mobile-first using fixed heuristics.
Aggregates age range, location type, and technology proficiency into a persona demographic profile.
Combines optional interview goals, needs, motivations, values, and quotes with behavioral patterns.
Produces persona scenarios, design implications, sample-size confidence labels, and formatted text or JSON output.
limitations: The included command uses built-in sample data and does not load supplied research datasets.
Each call creates one aggregate persona and does not discover multiple clusters within a dataset.
Archetypes, scenarios, and several frustrations come from fixed heuristics and templates.
Confidence labels use sample size only and do not represent statistical confidence or research validity.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Discovery Research
use_cases.description: Synthesize prepared behavioral records and interview notes into an evidence-linked draft persona for a discovery study.

use_cases.title: Guide Interface Concepts
use_cases.description: Translate a defined user segment into needs, frustrations, scenarios, and interface implications before concept design.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Segments
use_cases.description: Create comparable persona drafts for separately prepared segments when planning priorities with a cross-functional team.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Persona
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the persona generator with these prepared user records. Return the archetype, demographics, goals, frustrations, scenario, and confidence label: [records]
prompt_templates.scenario: Creating a first persona from structured research records.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interview Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a persona from these user records and interview insights. Separate observed inputs, heuristic conclusions, default content, and design implications: [data]
prompt_templates.scenario: Combining behavioral data with interview findings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Prepared Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate one persona for each prepared segment. Compare archetypes, behaviors, needs, frustrations, confidence labels, and design implications without merging records: [segments]
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluating distinct user groups for product planning.

prompt_templates.title: Review Segment Sensitivity
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a sensitivity review across alternative segment definitions. Identify changed classifications, stable findings, default assumptions, evidence gaps, and recommended validation work: [dataset]
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing whether persona conclusions depend on segmentation choices.

output_examples.input: Twenty-eight workplace users, mostly weekly desktop users, report sharing and reporting needs.
output: Scenario: Team collaboration with sharing and feedback tracking
Design implication: Support professional workflows and enterprise controls

output_examples.input: Twelve mobile users report daily use, quick interactions, and difficulty accessing desktop-only features.
output: Scenario: Complete a quick task while commuting
Design implication: Prioritize responsive, touch-optimized interactions

output_examples.input: Sixty daily desktop users each use more than ten distinct features and prioritize workflow speed.
output: Design implication: Provide shortcuts and power features

best_practices: Normalize fields and remove direct identifiers before providing research records.
Prepare meaningful segments separately because each generator call produces one aggregate persona.
Label defaults and heuristic conclusions, then validate them with participants and additional evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not present generated names, default quotes, or template scenarios as direct research evidence.
Do not treat one aggregate persona as proof of distinct market segments.
Do not describe the sample-size label as statistical confidence or validated research quality.

faq.question: Can the included command read my research file?
faq.answer: No. The command runs built-in sample data and only changes the output format when given the json argument.

faq.question: Can this skill create multiple personas automatically?
faq.answer: Not from one dataset. Prepare segments separately and run the generator once for each segment.

faq.question: Does it analyze raw interview transcripts?
faq.answer: No. Interview insights must be prepared as structured goals, needs, motivations, values, and quotes.

faq.question: How is the confidence label calculated?
faq.answer: It is low through 20 records, medium through 50 records, and high above 50 records.

faq.question: Does the script send or store research data?
faq.answer: No. It has no network or file-writing behavior, but supplied data and generated output remain visible in the execution environment.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
